page: Microsoft Azure D32pls_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Dplsv6 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs powered by a Microsoft Neoverse-N2 ARM processor operating at 3.4 GHz. The CPU architecture includes 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 128 MB L3 cache. The system is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, though it is premium storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the D32pls_v6 demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities and exceptional memory subsystem performance. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression both rank in the top 25%. Notably, memory bandwidth for large block read and write operations, along with the PassMark memory score and database operations, reach top-tier status in the top 10% of tested systems. Conversely, single-core metrics, such as stress-ng single-core CPU performance and Geekbench single-core scores, fall into the average range. Large-scale LLM inference, specifically prompt processing for 70B models, represents a performance bottleneck, registering in the bottom 10%.

The low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU offers a resource-dense, cost-efficient profile for compute-bound workloads that do not demand large memory footprints. However, the complete absence of local storage requires reliance on external premium storage, which may introduce latency tradeoffs. The server is well-characterized for multi-threaded tasks, software compilation with Clang, static web serving, and database operations, while being less optimal for memory-intensive applications or large-scale generative AI model execution.
